plugins.name: superpowers
plugins.description: It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for Claude to be able to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together. There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

plugins.name: caveman

This repo ships .codex/hooks.json, so caveman auto-starts when you run Codex inside this repo. The installed plugin itself gives you $caveman; copy the same hook into another repo if you want always-on behavior there too. caveman-commit and caveman-review are not in the Codex plugin bundle — use the SKILL.md files directly. ² Add the "Want it always on?" snippet below to those agents' system prompt or rule file if you want session-start activation. ³ Cursor and Windsurf receive the full SKILL.md with all intensity levels. Mode switching works on-demand via the skill; no slash command. ⁴ Available in Claude Code, but plugin install only nudges setup. Standalone install.sh / install.ps1 configures it automatically when no custom statusLine exists.

It doesn't reinvent Claude Code — it orchestrates it. /pw:generate uses the built-in Explore subagent for codebase analysis. /pw:migrate delegates to /batch for parallel file conversion. /pw:fix leverages /debug for trace inspection. Every skill builds on what Claude Code already does well. 55 ready-to-use test templates across 11 categories — authentication, CRUD, checkout, search, forms, dashboard, settings, onboarding, notifications, API testing, and accessibility. Each template includes TypeScript and JavaScript variants with parametrizable placeholders. Not generic stubs — real patterns like Stripe iframe handling, GraphQL mutation testing, and RBAC permission flows. 3 specialized agents handle complex planning before a single test is written: test-architect maps your application surface, test-debugger diagnoses flaky failures systematically, and migration-planner creates ordered conversion plans from Cypress or Selenium. 2 MCP integrations (TypeScript) connect to TestRail (8 tools) and BrowserStack (7 tools) for teams that need test management and cross-browser coverage. plugins.name: agenticmail
plugins.description: Give every Claude Code subagent its own real email address and phone number, all self hosted on the user's machine. AgenticMail runs a local mail server (Stalwart in a Colima or Docker container) so each agent has a working `<name>@localhost` inbox, an identity, an API key, and a persona. When a teammate is CC'd on an email they wake up as a Claude Code subagent under your existing Claude OAuth, read the full thread, decide if it is their turn, and either reply to all or stay silent. The thread is the workspace and the audit trail. There is no central orchestrator, no separate Anthropic key per agent, no data leaving your machine, and no polling because everything is push based over SSE. The plugin exposes three skills (`install`, `create-agent`, `coordinate`) that handle the one time bootstrap and let the host session kick off multi agent work with a single email. Behind the plugin sit five npm packages doing the real work: an Express API, an MCP server with 62 tools across email, SMS, contacts, drafts, templates, rules, search, scheduling, and agent coordination, a dispatcher daemon, a core SDK, and the CLI. Reliability rails include a per agent per thread wake budget that stops reply loops, a 60 second recent reply check in every persona so two agents who both think it is their turn back off, and an outbound content guard that holds risky outbound mail for owner approval. Tested on Node 22 and Node 25 with 429 passing tests across the workspace.

Cross-session memory changes the experience fundamentally. Without it, every session starts blind: the AI re-explores structure it already mapped, re-proposes approaches that were already rejected, re-debugs errors that were already solved. With the four-file memory stack, it arrives knowing what was tried, what was decided, and why — and builds forward instead of sideways. Five research-backed principles run throughout: *less is more* (minimal always-on instructions), *fresh context beats accumulated context* (subagents get clean scoped prompts, not polluted history), *compliance ≠ competence* (instructions must be carefully engineered, not just comprehensive), *verify your own reasoning* (multi-path self-consistency catches confident-but-wrong failures before they become expensive), and *accountability drives accuracy* (agents that know their output has real downstream consequences perform better).

Out of the box, Railguard comes with 29 default rules covering destructive operations like terraform destroy, rm -rf, DROP TABLE, and git force-push. It detects evasion attempts (base64 encoding, chr() construction, variable substitution, shell wrapping), restricts file access with path fencing (blocking ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, /etc), snapshots every file write for one-click rollback, and logs every decision to a structured audit trail. Everything is customizable through a simple railguard.yaml file in your project directory.

Each skill provides factual, up-to-date reference so agents can build correctly on Netlify without hallucinating APIs or config syntax.

plugins.name: healthclaw-guardrails
plugins.description: HealthClaw Guardrails is the security layer between AI agents and clinical FHIR data. Every agent read passes through PHI redaction (names truncated to initials, DOBs to year, identifiers masked). Every write requires an HMAC-signed step-up token with a 5-minute TTL. Clinical writes (Condition, MedicationRequest, DiagnosticReport) return HTTP 428 until a human confirms. Every access lands in an append-only audit trail scoped by tenant. Supports FHIR R4 US Core v9 (stable) and FHIR R6 v6.0.0-ballot3 (experimental). Proxies upstream FHIR servers (HAPI, Epic sandbox, Medplum via OAuth2 client-credentials, SMART Health IT) so the same guardrails apply whether you're on local SQLite or production EHRs. Bundled skills: fhir-r6-guardrails (core MCP + 14 tools), curatr (patient-facing data-quality evaluation and correction), fasten-connect (patient-authorized EHR ingestion + TEFCA), phi-redaction (HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification), fhir-upstream-proxy (vendor-neutral server proxy), healthex-export (portable health record export).

plugins.name: karma
plugins.description: Karma is a plugin for managing grants, projects, and funding programs on the Karma protocol. Discover funding opportunities across Web3 ecosystems, create and manage projects with milestones, track grant progress, and administer funding programs, all through natural conversation. No blockchain transactions needed; everything is gasless via API.

plugins.name: mine
plugins.description: Mines every Claude Code session into a local SQLite database and provides a /mine skill with 18+ natural language query intents. Track costs, tokens, tools, projects, errors, cache efficiency, and full-text search across all your past conversations. Features automatic session ingestion via hooks, error memory that warns when you repeat mistakes, cost anomaly detection, project/global scope detection, and API value tracking with subscription ROI comparisons. Zero external dependencies (stdlib Python only)

plugins.name: react-native-hifi
plugins.description: React Native HiFi is a complete React Native & Expo development workflow for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable "skills" and initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

plugins.name: riff
plugins.description: Riff is a plugin made up of nine opinionated skills for writing personal essays with Claude. The idea behind it is to treat writing with AI as a process to be supported instead of a product to be created, and to keep the writer in charge at every step of the way. Together, the skills form a pipeline so a user can start working with raw notes and get to a finished piece, but each skill also encourages time for pausing and reflection when appropriate. A persistent style profile built from a user's own writing keeps drafts in their voice across sessions, and the plugin is designed to handle personal material with care. The goal throughout is to make writing with Claude more fun and effective.

plugins.name: claude-english-buddy
plugins.description: A UserPromptSubmit hook that helps non-native English speakers improve while using Claude Code. Three modes dispatch automatically based on what you type: (1) correct — if your English prompt has errors, the hook fixes them and shows a per-line `wrong → right (reason)` diff so you learn the rule, not just the fix; (2) translate — if the input is non-English (Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, etc.), it's translated into natural English while preserving technical terms, file paths, and tool names; (3) refine — prefix `::` rewrites a rough idea into a precise prompt. Local JSONL history powers /today, /stats, /mistakes reports, and a /drill spot-quiz on top recurring patterns. Skills cover grammar, punctuation, tone, technical writing, and common L2-English mistakes.

plugins.name: docs-context
plugins.description: docs-context is the "Super Base Context" for Agent Coding: a structured replacement for single-file CLAUDE.md that separates project knowledge into five purpose-specific docs (architecture, modules, coding, tech-stack, decisions), loads only what the current task needs, and keeps those docs in sync with the code as a net-delta-triggered Write mode. Read mode fires before any non-trivial write/modify/refactor/design/plan task, grounding the agent in architectural constraints and conventions. Write mode fires once at the end of a task when landed changes (code, config, SQL, build scripts) differ from the doc state — no firing on read-only work, in-progress edits, or try-and-undo. Works across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity, Trae, Qoder via the standard SKILL.md format.

plugins.name: twilio-developer-kit

Includes skills for flow operations, debugging, and flow scaffolding. Requires a Flow Studio MCP subscription.

Built on the principles of Harness Engineering, it enforces a disciplined development workflow—from domain-driven scope refinement to strict TDD implementation and Socratic technical reviews—ensuring your AI assistant maintains architectural integrity, comprehensive test coverage, and persistent project memory throughout the entire software lifecycle.

Skills are scored after every execution — low scores trigger automatic repair, high scores lead to crystallization (locked, immutable versions). No external dependencies.

plugins.name: aura-frog

Aura Frog turns Claude Code into a disciplined development team — agents auto-select per task, tests are written before code (RED→GREEN→REFACTOR), and 3-tier rule architecture loads only what's needed (74% less context overhead). Includes 27 lifecycle hooks, 6 bundled MCP servers, git worktree isolation, phase checkpoints with rollback, collaborative multi-perspective planning, and a self-learning system that improves with every session. Zero config required — install and start your first workflow in 30 seconds.

plugins.name: cc-suite
plugins.description: cc-suite turns three CLI tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Google Gemini CLI) into one shared brain. Project context is written once in AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md just `@AGENTS.md` to import it. Skills live in `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` symlinks to it, so the same skill works in all three CLIs. Hooks defined for Claude Code are mirrored into Codex's hook system. MCP servers in .mcp.json are visible to all three. The Claude↔Codex delegation lane is bidirectional: from Claude, /cc-suite:audit, :implement, :verify, :review, :bug-analyze, and :review-plan all hand work to Codex and return structured results. Supersedes the separate cc-bridge and codex-toolkit plugins.

plugins.name: kindex
plugins.description: Kindex is a persistent knowledge graph for Claude Code. It turns Claude from a session-scoped tool into a project-scoped collaborator — capturing decisions, constraints, and context that survive across sessions, projects, and context resets. Memory plugins remember what happened. Kindex captures what it means and how it connects. Session 10 is as informed as session 1. Key features: session lifecycle management (tag_start, tag_resume, tag_end), constraint and watch enforcement across sessions, decision archaeology with reasoning preserved, and graph-structured context that surfaces insights by proximity rather than keyword search. Git blame tells you what changed. Kindex tells you why.

plugins.name: the-h-ai-k-u-method
plugins.description: H·AI·K·U (Human + AI Knowledge Unification) is a lifecycle orchestrator for structured AI-assisted work. Instead of loading instructions into the agent's context, H·AI·K·U drip-feeds one action at a time from a plan kept on disk — so runs survive context compaction, /clear, crashes, and even handoffs between humans. 24 built-in studios cover software, marketing, security, compliance, incident response, data pipelines, and more. Each stage has configurable autonomy (auto-advance, human review, or external sign-off), parallel adversarial review agents, and deterministic quality gates. The agent stays simple; the orchestrator holds the structure.

plugins.name: thumbgate

plugins.name: atelier-pipeline
plugins.description: Atelier Pipeline has two core systems: Multi-Agent Orchestration. Eleven specialized agent personas with clear responsibilities, strict boundaries, and independent quality verification. Eva orchestrates, Robert handles product, Sable designs UX, Sarah architects, Colby builds, Poirot blind-reviews every wave, Agatha documents, Ellis commits, Distillator compresses cross-phase artifacts, Sherlock investigates user-reported bugs, and Sentinel audits security (opt-in). Custom agents can be added via agent discovery. Specs get written, designs get validated, every change passes Eva's mechanical test gate plus Poirot blind review, and nothing ships without review. Works with Claude Code and Cursor. Atelier Brain. A persistent memory layer backed by PostgreSQL and vector embeddings that gives your agents institutional memory across sessions. Without it, every time you close a terminal you lose the architectural decisions that shaped your implementation, the user corrections that steered scope, the rejected alternatives that explain why you didn't go a different way, and the QA lessons that prevent recurring bugs. The brain captures all of this during pipeline runs and surfaces it automatically when agents need context. It includes write-time conflict detection, TTL-based knowledge decay, and background consolidation that synthesizes raw observations into higher-level insights. The pipeline works without the brain -- but with it, session 12 of a feature build has the same context as session 1.

Survives /clear commands and context compaction. Search across all sessions in a project or globally across every project. Auto-tags technical terms for discovery. Shares findings between parallel sessions via opt-in highlight connections. Includes a PostCompact nudge that automatically re-orients Claude after context loss. Claude talks to the extension over a local stdio MCP process and a localhost WebSocket (127.0.0.1:9847); the extension must have Agent Mode enabled. Supports feed browsing, post context, reply drafting with personas/moods, basic browser control (open tab, navigate, reload), and access checks. Works with Claude Code via the bundled plugin manifest and .mcp.json; also usable from Claude Desktop with a manual MCP entry. Requires Node.js 18+, the Socials extension, and (where applicable) a Socials plan that includes Agent Mode.

plugins.name: supergraph
plugins.description: Supergraph là plugin cho Claude Code, kết hợp hai phương pháp: - **Superpowers** (obra): Bắt buộc AI tuân theo quy trình làm việc có kỷ luật — brainstorm, plan, TDD, review. - **Code-review-graph** (tirth8205): Phân tích cấu trúc code bằng AST graph — blast radius, hub nodes, community detection, surprise scoring. ### Vấn đề supergraph giải quyết **Không có supergraph:** User: "Thêm authentication cho API" AI: *đọc toàn bộ 27,700 file* *viết code không có kế hoạch* *không viết test* *gửi PR* Tokens: ~443,200 Chất lượng: không đảm bảo **Có supergraph:** User: "Thêm authentication cho API" AI: 1. get_stats() → "Repo: 27,700 file, 12 communities, 8 languages" 2. Brainstorm → "JWT hay session? Endpoint nào?" 3. blast_radius(["src/auth/"]) → "15 file bị ảnh hưởng, 2 hub nodes" 4. Plan → 6 task, mỗi task 2-5 phút, có bước verify 5. TDD → viết test trước, implement sau, refactor 6. Auto-fix → chạy test + lint + review, tự sửa nếu lỗi 7. Review → blast_radius xác nhận tất cả file đã xử lý Tokens: ~4,260 Chất lượng: production-ready Tiết kiệm: 104x tokens ### Ngôn ngữ hỗ trợ | Ngôn ngữ | Test | Lint | Trạng thái | | -------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------- | ---------- | | Node.js / TypeScript | npm test, jest, vitest, mocha | eslint | Đầy đủ | | Flutter / Dart | flutter test | flutter analyze | Đầy đủ | | PHP | phpunit, pest | phpstan, phpcs | Đầy đủ |

plugins.name: repo-doctor
plugins.description: repo-doctor diagnoses README "shape problems" — the hero never lands, install-to-first-success buries the lede, the "what is this" sentence assumes prior context, the badge row is louder than the content — and produces a prioritized punch list a maintainer can act on in an afternoon. Read-only by default; opens a PR only when the user explicitly asks. Key features: - 9-criterion rubric scored 1–5 with cited line numbers and one-line fixes - Rubric weighting adapts to inferred repo category: library, CLI, framework, app, spec, or personal project - Audience inference (working developers, newcomers, maintainers, mixed) — catches the most common shape problem: README pitched at the wrong audience for its category - Punch list grouped P0 (blocking) / P1 (high-leverage) / P2 (nice-to-have) - Three operating modes (Auto / Semi-auto / Manual) with the same conversational density tradeoff as repo-visuals - Optional upstream PR with the punch list as the description; never auto-applies edits

plugins.name: repo-visuals
plugins.description: repo-visuals turns any open-source repo into a bespoke README hero — animated GIF or static PNG — through a structured discovery dialog. It scans the codebase, recommends a format that fits the repo's identity (terminal demo, product UI, brand wordmark, banner, diagram-as-hero), generates tailored HTML, previews it in your browser, and exports a retina-quality artifact ready to drop into the README. Key features: - Five-phase craft loop: discover → build → preview → export → output - Three operating modes (Auto / Semi-auto / Manual) that scale from "decide nothing" to "decide everything" - Format-aware: GIF for motion-worthy demos, PNG when stillness reads better, HTML when the README itself can host it - Retina capture via Puppeteer + ffmpeg; automatic file-size and dimension validation - Optional 4-rater scorecard (User / Claude / Code / AI-vision-blind) for measuring craft quality across runs - Optional upstream PR: detects ownership, forks if needed, opens a PR with alt-text included - Heroes already merged into HTMLHint, Terminal.Gui, ast-graph, and others

plugins.name: aomi-build
plugins.description: Use this to build agents hosted by Aomi Labs. An Aomi app is a platform-specific Rust API client compiled into an agentic application and loaded into the Aomi runtime to form a working crypto-trading agent. Apps are designed for crypto trading: the runtime supports native on-chain actions, so apps typically wrap complementary off-chain APIs from crypto platforms — CEXes, DEX aggregators, prediction markets, perp venues, oracles, social, on-chain analytics — to round out the agent's capabilities. aomi-build scaffolds new Aomi apps from API docs, OpenAPI/Swagger specs, SDK docs, runtime interfaces, or product requirements. It generates production-ready Rust SDK crates (lib.rs, client.rs, tool.rs) with tool schemas, preambles, host-interop flows, and validation steps — turning a vendor's full API surface into AI-agent-callable tools. Trigger when the user wants to scaffold a new Aomi app from an OpenAPI/Swagger spec, wrap a REST API as agent-callable tools, port an existing SDK to Aomi, generate a tool surface from product requirements, or extend the Aomi runtime with a new crypto integration. Prefers real product integrations over docs-only helpers whenever a callable surface exists. Output crates support sync HTTP, async tools (cancellation-safe via DynAsyncSink), proxy-unwrap (EIP-1967), and host-interop flows that route quote → approval → swap as multi-step transactions. Same runtime that aomi-transact drives — so an aomi-build-scaffolded app can be invoked alongside aomi-transact's on-chain primitives in the same agent session. --- About Aomi: Aomi Labs builds the native harness for blockchains, functioning like Claude Code on-chain. We specialize in executions against arbitrary protocols with non-custodial workflow, account abstraction, and full security via fork-chain simulation. Aomi also hosts agentic applications deployed and owned by developers, companies, and the agents themselves. We ship end-to-end: chat UI, agent Skills, and SDKs in TypeScript and Rust. Links: aomi.dev · x.com/aomi_labs · github.com/aomi-labs · npm: @aomi-labs/client, @aomi-labs/widget-lib · crates: aomi-sdk

plugins.name: aomi-transact
plugins.description: Use this skill to build natural-language crypto agents, web3 assistants, trading bots, blockchain MCPs, or Claude/Cowork plugins that read and write EVM chain state. Aomi turns user prompts ("swap 1 ETH for USDC", "open a 3x GMX long", "bet $100 yes on this Polymarket question") into wallet-signed transactions on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, and Linea — generic, non-custodial, with fork-chain simulation before every signature. Trigger when the user wants to: scaffold a crypto/DeFi agent, build an AI trading or wallet assistant, wrap an EVM protocol as MCP tools, create natural-language interfaces to APIs from Across / 1inch / GMX / Hyperliquid / Polymarket / Binance / OKX, or add on-chain execution to universal protocols (e.g. Uniswap / Aave / Lido / Morpho) to an agent stack. Aomi CLI connects to Aomi runtime reads and writes EVM chain state: stages calldata, simulates as a batch on a forked chain, and returns wallet requests for the user to sign. Works on any EVM contract via low-level primitives: ABI encoding (encode_and_call), fork-batch simulation (simulate_batch), staged-tx queueing (stage_tx), and wallet handoff with EIP-712 (commit_tx, commit_eip712) — including multi-step swap-approve-execute routing. Ships with 40+ tuned protocol apps and all on-chain smart contracts. Every action simulates first, batches when possible, and is signed by the end-user wallet — keys never leave.

plugins.description: Comprehensive security scanner for codebases. Scans for hardcoded secrets (30+ API key formats), injection flaws (SQLi, XSS, command injection, SSRF), authentication issues (JWT misuse, weak password hashing)misconfigurations (CORS, debug mode, insecure TLS, Docker/K8s), dependency risks, AI-specific vulnerabilities (prompt injection, API key exposure, excessive agent permissions), mobile security issues (Android/iOS), and data exposure (PII in logs, weak crypto). plugins.name: watch-video
plugins.description: watch-video gives Claude eyes and ears for any video — local files, public URLs (YouTube, Loom, Vimeo, TikTok, ~1,500 sites via yt-dlp), or Jira attachments fetched directly via API token. One command produces a complete evidence bundle: timestamped JPEG frames, a Whisper transcript (local faster-whisper or hosted Groq / OpenAI), optional OCR for on-screen text, and three report formats — report.md, self-contained report.html with base64-embedded frames, and corporate-friendly report.docx. Key features: - LLM-driven highlights: pass a prompt ("summarize the rate decision and inflation outlook", "identify the bug and when it occurs") and Claude picks the N most relevant moments with frame + reason + verbatim quote. - Smart dedup with perceptual hash + transcript-aware protection: typically drops 40-60% of redundant frames on screen recordings without losing narrated moments. - OCR for screen-recording UIs: Tesseract with 2x upscale + auto-invert + PSM 6, output to grep-able ocr.txt. - Per-step content-hash cache: re-runs are nearly free. - Opt-in Jira posting with a confirmation gate BEFORE any attachment upload — declining leaves the ticket untouched, no orphan state. - Batch mode for sprint retros: process a JQL query's worth of bug tickets in one command.

plugins.name: agented

Optimized for the model's cost model: fewer round trips per task (no Read-before-Edit; conflict responses carry the new content, so you reconcile in one call instead of pre-reading every time), tighter token budget (lean tab output, not JSON envelopes; ~5x denser than the built-in Read/Edit shape), inline LSP diagnostics on every save (gopls, rust-analyzer-with-clippy, tsserver+eslint findings come back as diag lines instead of round-tripping through cargo / go build), reactive drift detection (external editor or formatter writes are folded into the undo tree as new edits, not silently clobbered or lost), and a branching undo tree that remembers the branches the agent abandoned — because that's often where the interesting work was. plugins.name: slipstream
plugins.description: A tool that makes AI coding agents more effective for Dart and Flutter projects. AI agents working on Dart and Flutter run into two recurring problems. First, their training data has a cutoff — they'll reach for discontinued packages, pin outdated major versions, or produce subtly wrong API signatures that compile only after a correction loop. Second, Flutter development is inherently visual and stateful, and agents have no way to see a running app: they can't observe a layout failure, verify that a state change took effect, or confirm that a navigation worked. This tool addresses both. It adds hooks that catch stale package choices before they land in `pubspec.yaml`, an MCP server that retrieves accurate package API signatures directly from the local pub cache, and a suite of MCP commands for launching, inspecting, and interacting with a running Flutter app.

plugins.name: superfast
plugins.description: You know that moment when you've finally convinced your coding agent to build exactly what you want, only for it to instantly get hopelessly lost hallucinating dependencies in a 5,000-line codebase? Superfast fixes that. It starts by establishing your Context Memory. Before any brainstorming or planning occurs, it instantly triggers the FastMemory Build-Up Skill, recursively mapping your enterprise repository into a deterministic CBFDAE graph. Once your agent's cognitive map is established, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for Claude to be able to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

plugins.name: eight-eyes

Scope boundaries are enforced through deterministic Python hooks at the PreToolUse layer, not through prompt instructions. The 8 roles: implementer (scoped writes, no Bash), test-writer (test directories only), skeptic (blind read-only review), security auditor (read-only + approved scan commands), performance profiler (benchmarks in isolated worktree), accessibility checker (a11y tools + WCAG 2.1 checks), docs writer (doc paths only), and verifier (approved verification commands only). Features include parallel audit phase (4 review agents run concurrently), TDD mode (hook-level test-first enforcement), custom roles via manifest (--custom-role), REVIEW.md injection for project-specific review criteria, mission timeout and failure tracking. 96 tests. 100% Python stdlib. Zero external dependencies.

The agent cannot edit `src/` while requirements are still drafted, cannot commit a Wave with incomplete tasks, cannot push while the latest review verdict is MAJOR_ISSUES. - 3 spec reviewers (requirements / design / tasks) on fresh contexts, auto-iterating up to 3 times before a single user approval gate. Catches missing requirements and hallucinated acceptance criteria before any code is written. - Wave-based implementation: 1 Wave = 1 commit. Hooks cross-check the diff against each task's `_Files:_` meta to block phantom completion (marking `[x]` without an actual implementation). - 4-stage implementation review (spec-compliance / code-quality / security / adversarial) + per-issue validator on fresh contexts (memory: local, read-only) to filter false positives before findings reach the user. - Deterministic security detectors (semgrep SAST + osv-scanner CVE + npm registry hallucinated-package-check) injected as ground truth before LLM reviewers run. HIGH findings pin the verdict to MAJOR_ISSUES so the LLM cannot downgrade a real CVE. - Kuroko (黒衣) stance: zero side effects on projects that have not opted in (no `.mumei/current` = every Hook is a no-op). No telemetry, no writes outside `.mumei/`, no auto-commit, no auto-fix.

The result: a single greedy turn cannot spiral into a $30+ spend, sessions cannot silently accumulate cost over hours, and runaway burn rates are stopped before they hurt. Five configurable USD-based caps: • Per-session total spend • Per-step (prompt → response) cost • Trailing 5-minute burn rate • Per-step subagent fan-out count • Compaction gate (blocks the expensive context-compaction model call when limits are tight) Eleven slash commands for status, runtime config, pause/resume, and an optional bottom-row indicator. The indicator shows session spend, rate, current step cost, context %, and (on Claude.ai Pro/Max) 5-hour slot consumption with an estimated USD plan value. It composes with any existing statusLine (preserving your starship setup, etc.) or takes over the slot — your choice at install time. Pure Python 3 standard library. No runtime dependencies. No network calls. All enforcement is local; the plugin only reads the JSONL transcript Claude Code already writes. Screenshot: https://github.com/oggeh-dev/claude-cost-guard/blob/main/docs/indicator.png

plugins.name: forge
plugins.description: Description: Adversarial code hardening for Claude Code. Forge spawns two agents — a Builder and a Breaker — that iterate against each other until the code is unbreakable. The Builder implements a feature, the Breaker writes adversarial tests to prove bugs, and the Builder must fix the implementation without deleting or weakening the tests. The loop continues until the Breaker can't produce a failing test. The result is battle-tested code with a permanent adversarial test suite. Key features: - Evidence-based, not opinion-based. Every issue the Breaker raises must have a failing test that proves the bug. No test, no break. This eliminates false positives and subjective feedback. - Iterative adversarial loop. Builder and Breaker are separate agents that go back and forth for up to N rounds. The Builder cannot dismiss feedback; it must make the failing tests pass. - Adversarial tests are permanent. The Breaker's tests stay in the repo under tests/adversarial/ as a regression suite. Future changes are protected by the same tests that originally caught the bugs. - Automatic checkpoint. Creates a git tag before starting so the entire forge session can be rolled back with one command. - Configurable rounds. Default 5 rounds, adjustable with --rounds N. Stops early if the Breaker can't find issues. - Auto-detects project stack. Reads config files to determine language, test framework, and conventions. Works with Python, TypeScript, Rust, Go, Ruby, and anything with a test runner.

plugins.name: icf-classification
plugins.description: Access WHO ICF (International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health) codes. ICF complements ICD diagnosis codes by describing how health conditions affect a person's functioning in daily life - covering body functions, body structures, activities/participation, and environmental factors.

plugins.name: ido4specs
plugins.description: ido4specs is the bridge between a strategic spec and GitHub issues. It analyzes your codebase, decomposes capabilities into implementation tasks with effort, risk, type, and dependency metadata, and produces a structurally-validated technical spec any downstream tool can consume. Key features: - Code-grounded decomposition - parallel Explore subagents ground every task in concrete files, services, and patterns from your actual codebase (not fabricated from the spec) - Structured output enforced by a bundled zero-dependency parser - every task carries effort (S/M/L/XL), risk (low → critical), type (feature/infrastructure), AI-suitability (full/assisted/pair/human), and dependency graph - Two-layer validation - deterministic structural parser + independent qualitative review before handoff Built for tech leads, staff engineers, and founder-engineers who want to skip the manual decomposition tax.

plugins.name: indian-banking-drafting
plugins.description: For every recovery counsel, bank panel advocate, borrower's counsel, and insolvency professional practising before India's banking-litigation forums — the Debts Recovery Tribunals, the Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal, the National Company Law Tribunal (for IBC matters), CMM / DM courts for SARFAESI Section 14 possession, and civil courts of pecuniary jurisdiction — this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises drafting across the full Indian banking-litigation surface. Case-config-aware: forum, security position, NPA classification, demand-notice trajectory, default trigger, and security-document inventory are user-supplied. Battle-tested for DRT Original Applications under Section 19 RDDBFI Act 1993, SARFAESI Section 13(2) demand notices, SARFAESI Section 17 Securitisation Applications, SARFAESI Section 14 CMM / DM possession applications, Negotiable Instruments Act Section 138 complaints and reply notices, civil recovery suits under Order 7 / Order 37 CPC, IBC Section 7 financial-creditor applications before the NCLT, IBC Section 95 personal-guarantor insolvency applications, and DRAT appeals under Section 20 RDDBFI Act 1993. Six-agent drafting pipeline + shared banking drafting base with RDDBFI Act 1993, SARFAESI Act 2002, Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, Banking Regulation Act 1949, RBI Master Directions, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 encoded. The finished product is a forum-ready pleading the chamber can file at the DRT, NCLT, or Magistrate's Court the same day.

plugins.name: indian-company-drafting
plugins.description: For every company-law litigator, insolvency professional, and corporate counsel practising before India's company-law tribunals — every National Company Law Tribunal bench across India and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (Principal Bench and Chennai Bench) — this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises Companies Act and IBC drafting. Case-config-aware: forum, share-capital structure, board composition, alleged-oppression acts, scheme terms, capital-reduction arithmetic, strike-off history, investigation grounds, operational-debt particulars, corporate-applicant financial distress, and the NCLT order under appeal are user-supplied. Battle-tested for Sections 241 / 242 / 244 (oppression and mismanagement), Section 245 (class action), Sections 230-232 (compromise / arrangement / amalgamation / scheme), Section 66 (reduction of share capital), Section 252 (revival of a struck-off company), Section 213 (investigation into the affairs of a company), IBC Section 9 (operational-creditor CIRP application), IBC Section 10 (corporate-applicant self-initiation), Companies Act Section 421 (NCLAT appeal from NCLT order), and IBC Section 61 (NCLAT appeal from NCLT order under the IBC). Six-agent drafting pipeline + shared company drafting base with the Companies Act 2013, IBC 2016, NCLT Rules 2016, NCLAT Rules 2016, IBBI Regulations, Secretarial Standards SS-1 / SS-2, Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules 2016, Companies (Inspection, Investigation and Inquiry) Rules 2014, BNSS 2023, and BSA 2023 encoded. Companies Act 1956 → 2013 transition discipline encoded in the Verifier. The finished product is a Tribunal-ready petition or appeal the chamber can lodge at the NCLT or NCLAT Registry the same day.

plugins.name: indian-consumer-drafting
plugins.description: For every consumer counsel and medical-negligence advocate practising before India's three-tier Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions — District Commission for claims up to ₹1 crore, State Commission for claims of ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore, and the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission for claims above ₹10 crore — this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises drafting under the Consumer Protection Act 2019. Case-config-aware: the parties' Commission tier, pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction, deficiency-of-service / defect-in-goods / unfair-trade-practice / product-liability character, medical-negligence anchor (Jacob Mathew, Martin F. D'Souza, Kusum Sharma, the Bolam standard), Section 69 limitation anchor, and accompanying-application set are user-supplied. Battle-tested for District Section 35 Complaints, State Section 47 originals, NCDRC Section 58 originals, Medical Negligence Complaints, Product Liability Actions under Sections 82-87, Unfair Trade Practice Complaints, Appeals under Sections 41 and 51, Revisional Applications under Section 67, and Execution under Sections 71-72. Six-agent drafting pipeline + shared consumer drafting base with the Consumer Protection Act 2019, CDRC Rules 2020, E-Commerce Rules 2020, Sale of Goods Act 1930, Indian Medical Council (Professional Conduct) Regulations 2002, New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules 2019, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 encoded. The finished product is a Commission-ready complaint or appeal the chamber can sign and file across the counter the same day.

plugins.name: indian-contracts-drafting
plugins.description: For every transactional advocate, in-house counsel, and law-firm associate who drafts the day-to-day contracts that underpin Indian commerce — from a startup's MSA to a family-business shareholders agreement to the last Will of a senior citizen — this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises commercial-contract drafting under Indian law. Contract-config-aware: the structural skeleton is uniform across contract types; governing law, seat of arbitration, courts of exclusive jurisdiction, stamp-duty State, and registration State are user-supplied. Battle-tested for Master Service Agreement, Non-Disclosure Agreement, Employment Agreement and Independent Contractor agreement, Lease Deed and Leave & License agreement, Sale Deed of immovable property, General and Special Power of Attorney (post-Suraj Lamp discipline), Shareholders Agreement (Companies Act 2013 + AoA alignment), Last Will and Testament, Loan Agreement, and standalone Arbitration Agreement. Six-agent drafting pipeline (Reader → Format → Drafter → Verifier → Refiner → Overseer) + shared contract drafting base with the Indian Contract Act 1872, Transfer of Property Act 1882, Registration Act 1908, Indian Stamp Act 1899, Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, and DPDP Act 2023 discipline encoded. The finished product is an execution-ready contract or instrument the chamber can stamp, sign, and execute the same day.

plugins.name: indian-family-drafting
plugins.description: For every advocate practising before India's Family Courts under the Family Courts Act 1984 and the matrimonial-jurisdiction tier of District Courts, this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises drafting across India's plural personal-law regimes — Hindu Marriage Act 1955, Special Marriage Act 1954, Indian Divorce Act 1869, Muslim Personal Law, Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act 1936 — and the State Family-Court overlay applicable to the parties. The structural skeleton is uniform; personal-law and State overlay are supplied by the user via a family-config file. Battle-tested for Divorce (HMA / SMA / IDA), Judicial Separation, Restitution of Conjugal Rights, Nullity of Marriage, Maintenance (Section 125 BNSS + Section 24 HMA + Section 18 HAMA), Custody and Guardianship (Guardians and Wards Act 1890 + Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956), Domestic Violence reliefs (PWDVA 2005), and Adoption (HAMA / Juvenile Justice Act 2015). Six-agent drafting pipeline (Reader → Format → Drafter → Verifier → Refiner → Overseer) and shared family pleading base. The finished product is a filing-ready petition, application, or written statement the counsel can lodge at the Family Court the same working day.

plugins.name: indian-ip-drafting
plugins.description: For every intellectual-property litigation advocate practising before India's IP forums — the Intellectual Property Rights Division of the Delhi, Madras, Calcutta, and Bombay High Courts (post-IPAB abolition under the Tribunals Reforms Act 2021), the Commercial Division, Commercial Courts under the Commercial Courts Act 2015, and District Courts of competent pecuniary jurisdiction — this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises drafting across India's full IP-litigation surface. Case-config-aware: forum, nature of the IP right (copyright / trade mark / patent / design / passing-off), infringement-mode allegations, prior-use evidence inventory, and registration particulars are user-supplied. Battle-tested for copyright infringement suits under Section 51 read with Section 55 Copyright Act 1957, fair-dealing defences under Section 52, trade mark infringement suits under Sections 29 / 134 / 135 Trade Marks Act 1999, common-law passing-off suits, trade mark rectification applications under Section 57 (post-IPAB-abolition to the High Court IP Division), patent infringement suits under Sections 104 and 108 Patents Act 1970, patent revocation applications under Section 64 (post-IPAB-abolition to the High Court IP Division), design piracy suits under Section 22 and Section 19 cancellation under the Designs Act 2000, John Doe / Ashok Kumar / Anton Piller applications under Order 39 CPC, and interim injunction applications applying the American Cyanamid / Gujarat Bottling framework. Six-agent drafting pipeline + shared IP drafting base with the Copyright Act 1957, Trade Marks Act 1999, Patents Act 1970 (as amended), Designs Act 2000, Tribunals Reforms Act 2021, Delhi High Court IPRD Rules 2022, Madras High Court IPRD Rules, Commercial Courts Act 2015, CPC Order 39, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 encoded. The finished product is a Division-ready or Court-ready suit, application, or rectification petition the chamber can file the same day.

plugins.name: indian-mact-drafting
plugins.description: For every advocate practising before India's Motor Accident Claims Tribunals — the tribunal-tier where every road accident in India ultimately lands for compensation — and before the High Court on Section 173 appeals and the Magistrate's Court on the rash / negligent-driving trial under BNSS 2023, this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises the full motor-accident litigation surface. Case-config and state-config-aware: forum (MACT of the territorial district, High Court for Section 173 appeal, Magistrate Court for the rash / negligent-driving prosecution, Collector for Section 174 recovery), accident-trigger date, claimant composition (legal representatives of the deceased / injured claimant / property-damage claimant), vehicle particulars, FIR particulars, insurer particulars, Sarla Verma + Pranay Sethi multiplier inputs, and State Motor Vehicles Rules variations are user-supplied. Battle-tested for Section 166 fault-based claims, Section 164 lump-sum claims (post-2019 amendment, replacing Section 163A), Section 161 solatium / hit-and-run claims, Section 147 / 149 third-party insurance pleadings, interim compensation applications, Section 173 appeals to the High Court, claim-award execution, Employees' Compensation Act 1923 claims, rash / negligent-driving defence under BNSS 2023, and Section 174 recovery as arrears of land revenue. Six-agent drafting pipeline + shared MACT drafting base with the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (as amended 2019), Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989, applicable State MV Rules, Employees' Compensation Act 1923, BNS / BNSS / BSA 2023, the Sarla Verma multiplier doctrine, and the Pranay Sethi constitution-bench future-prospects reform encoded. The finished product is a Tribunal-ready claim petition or appeal the team can lodge the same day.

plugins.name: indian-property-drafting
plugins.description: For every conveyancing advocate, transactional lawyer, sub-registrar's panel advocate, and family-property counsel practising across India — wherever a Gift Deed, Exchange Deed, Release Deed, Trust Deed, Wakf Deed, Easement Deed, Partition Deed, Family Settlement Deed, Mortgage Deed, or Title Investigation Report has to be drawn for registration before the State Sub-Registrar — this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises non-commercial conveyancing and family-property drafting. (Complements indian-contracts-drafting, which covers the commercial-contracts side.) State-config-aware: the applicable State Stamp Act schedule, Registration Act 1908 compulsory-registration position, Sub-Registrar office, Ready Reckoner / Market Value rates, mutation entry route, and State-specific instrument variations are user-supplied via a deed-config file and the relevant state-config exemplar. Battle-tested for Gift Deeds under Sections 122-129 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, Exchange Deeds under Sections 118-121 TPA, Release Deeds, Private Trust Deeds under the Indian Trusts Act 1882, Wakf Deeds under the Wakf Act 1995 read with the Mussalman Wakf Validating Act 1913, Easement Deeds under the Indian Easements Act 1882, Partition Deeds (private partition between coparceners / co-owners outside court), Family Settlement Deeds (Hindu family settlement / consent-of-heirs settlement), Registered Mortgage Deeds under Section 59 TPA, and Title Investigation Reports (title chain + encumbrance + marketable title opinion for due diligence). Six-agent drafting pipeline + shared property drafting base with the Indian Contract Act 1872, Transfer of Property Act 1882, Registration Act 1908, Indian Stamp Act 1899, applicable State Stamp Acts, Indian Easements Act 1882, Indian Trusts Act 1882, Wakf Act 1995, Hindu Succession Act 1956, Indian Succession Act 1925, Mussalman Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1937, Suraj Lamp (2012) discipline, and Section 53A TOPA agreement-to-sell discipline encoded. The finished product is a Sub-Registrar-ready deed the chamber can stamp, sign, and register the same day.

plugins.name: indian-tax-drafting
plugins.description: For every direct-tax litigator and chartered-accountant counsel practising before India's tax appellate hierarchy — Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals), Income-tax Appellate Tribunal, High Court Tax Bench under Section 260A, the PCIT / CIT for registration and revision, and the Dispute Resolution Panel — this open-source Claude Code plugin standardises drafting under the Income-tax Act 1961. Case-config-aware: structural skeletons follow the statutory Form layouts (Form 35 under Rule 45, Form 36 under Rule 47, Form 10A under Rule 17A); the forum, assessment year, financial year, limitation anchor, assessment-order vintage (pre-Finance-Act-2021 reassessment regime vs Section 148A regime), faceless-vs-physical jurisdiction, and demand-notice / penalty-notice trajectory are user-supplied. Battle-tested for CIT(Appeals) Form 35 appeals under Section 246A, ITAT Form 36 appeals under Section 253, High Court appeals on substantial questions of law under Section 260A, Section 12A / 12AB charitable-trust registrations via Form 10A, objections to Section 148A(b) reassessment show-cause notices, replies to Section 271 / 270A penalty notices, objections to Section 263 PCIT / CIT revisions, taxpayer-initiated revisions before the PCIT / CIT under Section 264, replies to Section 201 / 201(1A) TDS-default proceedings, and DRP objections under Section 144C. Six-agent drafting pipeline + shared tax drafting base with the Income-tax Act 1961, Income-tax Rules 1962, ITAT Rules 1963, Faceless Appeal Scheme 2021, Faceless Assessment Scheme 2020, Finance Act 2021 reassessment overhaul (Section 148A), CBDT public-domain Circulars, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 encoded. The finished product is a forum-ready appeal, reply, or registration application the chamber can lodge the same day.

plugins.name: intention-driven-design
plugins.description: Intention-Driven Design (IDD) is a methodology for building software where every artifact traces back to a declared human intent. Code is a downstream consequence of intent, never the starting point. We allow change, but we do not allow drift.

plugins.name: jucho-kun
plugins.description: Automates the preliminary investigation phase for Japanese real estate disclosure documents (重要事項説明書). Given a property address, it generates a complete due diligence checklist, extracts key facts from PDFs (registry certificates, urban planning maps, hazard maps), and outputs a structured Excel investigation report. Built for licensed real estate appraisers and agents (宅建士・不動産鑑定士).

plugins.name: kansei-link
plugins.description: Discover 301 SaaS/API services with trust scores and auto-invocation skill. 91-96% token savings vs web research.

plugins.name: keep-alive
plugins.description: A Claude Code plugin that prevents your machine from sleeping during long Claude Code sessions. Inspired by GitHub Copilot CLI's /keep-alive command.

plugins.name: keep-awake
plugins.description: Prevents your computer from sleeping while Claude Code is working. Cross-platform support for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Activates automatically on prompt submission and tool use, auto-expires after 30 minutes of inactivity, and cleans up on session end — no orphaned processes.

plugins.name: klarity
plugins.description: Explore your org's processes and drive AI transformation

plugins.name: koko-credit-card-plugin
plugins.description: Skill to help Claude run credit card related workflows like 'Review my cards', 'Which card should i use', 'Help me find a new card'

plugins.name: kotlinsense
plugins.description: Kotlin language server for Claude Code. Automatically injects type-error diagnostics, missing import detection, and null safety violations into Claude's context after every .kt file edit — no manual compile step needed. Works for any Kotlin or Android project.

plugins.name: launchpad
plugins.description: The most comprehensive agentic coding harness for Claude Code that works for both greenfield and brownfield projects. Drops 38 slash commands, 36 sub-agents, and 16 skills into any repo to give Claude Code full project context, run it through structured shape → plan → build → review → ship loops, and enforce multi-agent quality gates before any change reaches main. Works in any existing TypeScript, Python, Go, Django, or polyglot repo — install the plugin and run /lp-kickoff to start.

plugins.name: lean
plugins.description: Plan tasks with optimal model routing to minimize token usage. Breaks work into steps, assigns each the right model (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus), adds quality gates between stages, persists the plan to file, and reports savings after execution. Includes a companion hook for always-on model suggestions. Use /lean before complex tasks.

plugins.name: learning-toolkit
plugins.description: A Claude Code plugin that teaches you through questions instead of answers. Two skills — learn guides you through code understanding with four modes (Socratic questioning, concept chunking, gap analysis, and syntax hints), while prompt-check catches when you're prompting poorly and coaches you toward better questions. Both auto-trigger based on how you're asking, so you don't need to invoke them explicitly.

plugins.name: lesson-skill-loop
plugins.description: Turn development lessons into reusable skills — analyze tag patterns, propose skill creation, sync improvements, check health, and map traceability

plugins.name: linkedin-scam-detector
plugins.description: Detect fake recruiter emails and job offer scams. Requires Claude Code and the Claude in Chrome extension. Opens your email in the browser, analyzes the message, verifies the sender domain and email format against company directories, checks the recruiter's LinkedIn profile directly, searches for the job posting on the company's careers page, and finds a verified phone number to call back — with warnings about spoofed caller ID.

plugins.name: liquid-dev
plugins.description: Liquid Dev gives Claude Code deep knowledge of Shopify's Liquid templating language, Online Store 2.0 theme architecture, and modern theme development workflows. It bundles a complete Liquid reference (objects, tags, filters, section schemas, metafields, dynamic sources, performance patterns), a theme development guide covering Shopify CLI, Dawn customization, settings schemas, and deployment — plus an opinionated Shopify developer agent that builds production themes with vanilla CSS/JS, merchant-friendly settings, and performance-first defaults. Built by a developer with 13+ years of Shopify experience who got tired of watching AI hallucinate Liquid syntax.

plugins.name: llm-secure-patterns
plugins.description: Secure design patterns for Claude Code LLM applications: external content ingestion, endpoint hardening, output validation, system prompt design, and multi-agent action surface control. Maps to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025.

plugins.name: local-mcp
plugins.description: Connect Claude Code to Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Teams, OneDrive, and 80+ macOS tools. All data stays on your Mac — no cloud, no tokens, no API keys

plugins.name: logfire
plugins.description: Pydantic Logfire observability platform integration. Query traces, monitor application performance, analyze logs, and debug issues directly from Claude Code.

plugins.name: lookout
plugins.description: A Claude Code plugin that keeps your AI toolchain current. Before you start new work, Lookout catches you up on everything that changed — then helps you incorporate what matters.

plugins.name: lorkinsey
plugins.description: Structured product thinking sessions modeled after YC office hours. Helps you stress-test new ideas, product directions, and "is this worth building" decisions through research-backed interrogation — not cheerleading. Anti-sycophantic by design: takes positions, challenges assumptions, and demands specifics before letting you move forward.

plugins.name: magellan
plugins.description: Enterprise knowledge discovery and process repository. Point Magellan at a folder of collected materials — code, documents, meeting transcripts, API specs, diagrams — and it builds a structured, queryable knowledge graph organized by business domain. Then use the knowledge graph to research, plan, and execute work with full context at every stage.

plugins.name: marcopolo
plugins.description: MarcoPolo is a data computer that connects to your databases, warehouses, cloud storage, and SaaS applications, and provides a workspace where AI can query, correlate, analyze, and act on that data. The MarcoPolo plugin is the most effective way to connect Claude to this computer - it bundles the MCP connection with skills and a subagent that guide Claude through proven data workflows.

plugins.name: marketing-for-life-sciences
plugins.description: A life sciences adaptation of the marketing plugin for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medtech teams. Extends the full general marketing toolkit with regulatory compliance (FDA/EMA), MLR review workflows, HCP engagement, KOL strategy, congress marketing, and pharma-specific KPIs. Designed primarily for Cowork, also compatible with Claude Code.

plugins.name: mcp-skill-search
plugins.description: A "ToolSearch for skills" — searches your SKILL.md files by keyword, exact name, or required-term filter so the model can fetch full skill descriptions on demand. Mirrors Claude Code's internal ToolSearch scoring algorithm 1:1, but for skills instead of MCP tools. Pairs with two bundled slash-commands: /optimize-skill-context sets SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET=1 to free Claude Code's ~1% skill-description budget (forcing names-only mode), and /restore-skill-descriptions reverses it. Slash-commands keep working; descriptions are fetched on demand via skill_search when relevant. Repo-aware: skills under the current git-root's .claude/skills/ get a +5 score boost over same-named skills from other repos, so search ranking respects which project you're working in.

plugins.name: mcp-yoshi
plugins.description: Real-time security filter for MCP tool communications. Works as a Claude Code hook to inspect all data sent to and received from MCP servers. Detects prompt injection, API key leakage, tool poisoning, ASCII smuggling, SSRF, Base64-encoded payloads, and Rug Pull attacks. Provides PASS/WARN/BLOCK decisions with per-server configuration, allowlisting, and logging. Zero dependencies, ~60ms latency.

plugins.name: memo-yoshi
plugins.description: Sticky notes for Claude Code. Write memos in a Markdown file — URLs, ideas, TODOs, anything. Claude reads, organizes by category, and acts on them (opens URLs, runs checks, marks done). No app needed, just a Markdown file + a skill definition.

plugins.name: memoriant-temporal-planner-skill
plugins.description: Dependency-ordered task planning and execution for Claude Code. Builds task DAGs with temporal constraint resolution, identifies critical paths, enables parallel execution where dependencies allow, and tracks progress with ETA estimation.

plugins.name: memorydetective
plugins.description: Hunt iOS memory leaks and investigate runtime performance from inside Claude Code. memorydetective bundles an MCP server with 28 tools for analyzing .memgraph and .trace files, plus a /perf-investigate skill that routes you to the right playbook based on symptoms (leak, hang, jank, slow launch). Key features: - 34-pattern retain-cycle classifier covering SwiftUI (incl. @Observable, SwiftData, NavigationStack), Swift Concurrency, Combine, UIKit, Core Data, RxSwift, Realm, and Coordinator pattern - Every classification ships fixHint + staticAnalysisHint + a Swift before/after fixTemplate snippet - Trace analysis: hangs, animation hitches, allocations, app launch, time profile - compareTracesByPattern for CI gating against perf regressions - 5 SourceKit-LSP-backed Swift source-bridging tools (find references, hover, definitions) - macOS unified logging (logShow / logStream) - 5 slash commands for direct invocation: /investigate-leak, /investigate-hangs, /investigate-jank, /investigate-launch, /verify-cycle-fix Reads memgraphs exported from Xcode's Memory Graph Debugger and traces from xctrace. Ships as both a Claude Code plugin and a standalone npm package, so the same MCP server works in Cursor, Cline, Claude Desktop, and Continue.

plugins.name: meta-learn
plugins.description: AI-powered interactive learning coach that helps users master any topic 10x faster. Features knowledge maps, Feynman sparring, Socratic drilling, instant feedback, and cross-domain transfer. Supports Chinese and English.

plugins.name: mission
plugins.description: Break large coding tasks into milestones with validation gates and file-based state that survives context resets. Six commands cover the full lifecycle: plan the work, execute milestone-by-milestone, resume with fresh context after /clear, check progress, adjust the plan mid-flight, and run acceptance criteria. Built on Boyd's OODA loop — every milestone is an observe-orient-decide-act cycle, so the agent stays grounded in reality instead of drifting.

plugins.name: mulmocast
plugins.description: MulmoCast skills for Claude Code — create, narrate, and extend video presentations from any input

plugins.name: music-catalog-diligence
plugins.description: Music Catalog Diligence helps catalog buyers, sellers, and financing teams review music catalog deals faster and with better evidence. It turns messy data rooms into source-cited workpapers by normalizing royalty statements, checking rights and metadata gaps, analyzing NPS/NLS, flagging diligence risks, and preparing buyer, seller, or lender-ready deal packages.

plugins.name: neko-gundan
plugins.description: Multi-agent orchestration framework for Claude Code. Organizes Claude into a hierarchical cat team — Oyakata-neko (General/Opus) plans strategy, Shigoto-neko (Manager/Sonnet) breaks down tasks, and Genba-neko (Worker/Sonnet) executes in parallel. Features auto-scaling from solo to battalion based on task complexity, quality gates with structured review protocols, and bidirectional feedback loops.

plugins.name: neko-harness-doctor
plugins.description: Diagnose your Claude Code harness (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, .mcp.json, hooks, skills, memory, MCP servers, and workflow) against 25 anti-pattern indicators. Outputs an S–E overall grade, per-category scores, violations with evidence citations, and prioritized Quick Wins. Includes an interactive fix flow: `--fix-mode propose` emits structured JSON proposals that Claude Code applies via the Edit tool with per-item user approval. Deterministic (no LLM — grep/AST/JSON only), zero runtime dependencies, bilingual (Japanese default, English via `--lang en`). When installed as a plugin, the bundled skill auto-triggers on natural-language requests like "diagnose my harness" and exposes `/neko-harness-doctor` as a slash command.

plugins.name: nerdygeek
plugins.description: NerdyGeek gives Claude Code a version-aware documentation lookup tool that dynamically discovers official docs for frameworks and libraries, retrieves the most relevant sections, filters noise, and returns structured answers with source links and code examples. It is designed to help coding agents recover from uncertainty quickly and continue working with current documentation instead of stale assumptions.

plugins.name: next-js-e-commerce-seo-skills-for-ai-coding-assistants
plugins.description: SEO skills for AI coding assistants working on Next.js e-commerce sites. 10 auto-triggered skills cover metadata, structured data (JSON-LD), hreflang for multi-locale sites, image optimization, Core Web Vitals, URL structure, crawlability, internal linking, redirects, and e-commerce page patterns. 2 audit commands (/seo-audit-page, /seo-audit-component) produce PASS/WARN/FAIL checklists. Skills are advisory — they inform the assistant about SEO best practices so it can give good advice when asked, without making unsolicited code changes. Works with Next.js 15.x and 16.x, App Router and Pages Router.

plugins.name: nexusfeed-ltl-fuel-surcharges
plugins.description: Real-time LTL freight carrier fuel surcharge rates for AI agents. Covers 11 carriers (ODFL, Saia, Estes, ABF, R+L, TForce, XPO, SEFL, Averitt, FedEx, UPS). Every response includes a _verifiability block with extraction confidence, source timestamp, and evidence URL. Installed via uvx, authenticated with MCP_API_KEY env var.

plugins.name: notify-sounds
plugins.description: Plays system sounds in Claude Code when a task finishes or when permission is needed, so you don't have to keep watching the terminal. Cross-platform: macOS (afplay), Linux (PulseAudio/PipeWire), Windows (PowerShell SoundPlayer), with terminal-bell fallback. Sub-agent stops are skipped to avoid noise during multi-agent workflows.

plugins.name: npm-postinstall-attack-scanner
plugins.description: Detect npm supply chain attacks that use the postinstall + hidden dependency pattern to deliver malware. Built in response to the axios maintainer account takeover (2026-03-31). Scans lockfiles, ode_modules, postinstall scripts, version ranges, and npm cache across 5 phases. Returns actionable remediation steps when issues are found.

plugins.name: numeric-mcp-toolkit
plugins.description: Skills for the Numeric's MCP. Purpose-built workflows for accounting teams — rec workbooks, department anomaly scanning, cross-workspace close dashboards, audit evidence exports, close pulse reporting, consolidated flux commentary, financial metrics, clean report exports, and executive/board-ready reports.

plugins.name: olostep
plugins.description: Turn any website into clean, LLM-ready markdown or structured data. Olostep integrates powerful web scraping, crawling, search, and AI-powered answers directly into Claude Code. Scrape single pages, crawl entire sites, map site structures, batch-process thousands of URLs, and search the web — all with automatic JavaScript rendering, anti-bot bypasses, and real-time extraction built in. The plugin includes an AI answers tool that goes beyond scraping: describe what you need in plain language and Olostep searches the live web, synthesizes the results, and returns a source-backed answer with structured JSON output — no URLs required. How to use: After installing, set your OLOSTEP_API_KEY environment variable. Then use these commands to get started: /olostep:scrape — Extract any webpage as clean markdown, HTML, or structured JSON. /olostep:crawl — Crawl and extract content from an entire website. /olostep:search — Search the web and get deduplicated results with titles and descriptions. /olostep:map — Discover all URLs on a site instantly. /olostep:answer — Ask a question in plain language and get a source-backed answer from live web data. /olostep:batch — Scrape up to 10,000 URLs in a single async job. You can also use Olostep's tools directly in conversation: ask Claude to scrape a URL, search for recent information, extract structured data with a custom schema, or research competitors across multiple sites.

plugins.name: onecli
plugins.description: Connect AI agents to external APIs with zero credential management. The OneCLI gateway transparently proxies all HTTPS traffic and injects stored credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, AWS signatures) into outbound requests. Supports 40+ services including GitHub, Gmail, Google Calendar, Jira, AWS, Stripe, Datadog, and more. Policy rules enforce block, rate limit, and manual approval at the gateway level.

plugins.name: preserve-session
plugins.description: Preserves Claude Code session history across project directory renames, moves, and copies by assigning each project a path-independent UUID and maintaining a global registry mapping UUID to current path. Addresses a long-standing pain point: --resume and --continue silently lose session history when paths change. Closes anthropics/claude-code#5768; also tracked in #38089, #28745, #26766, #27883. Commands: /preserve-session:fix recovers sessions after rename/move (with copy detection and automatic .jsonl merge on destination collision), /preserve-session:inherit copies session history from another registered project, /preserve-session:doctor diagnoses hash/registry state and slug collisions including non-ASCII path issues on macOS, /preserve-session:uninstall removes all preserve-session data with a preview-then-confirm safety pattern. A SessionStart hook auto-initializes .claude/hash.txt on first run — zero manual setup. Demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lWMrzASG7_o Quality signals: 24 verified test scenarios (rename, move, copy, slug collision, non-ASCII paths, registry corruption recovery, full --resume E2E). Atomic registry writes via fcntl.LOCK_EX + tempfile.mkstemp + os.replace. NFC slug normalization to match Claude Code's path encoding on macOS. Python heredoc isolation against shell injection. Symlink-safe uninstall (isinstance/dict guards). Shared helpers in hooks/common.sh with cross-platform Python discovery and uuidgen fallback. Full design rationale, security notes, and test plan are in two related submissions: • https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/39148 (initial bundled-plugin attempt; comprehensive design + 24-item test plan with collapsible sections) • https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/pull/1347 (auto-closed by submission bot; retained as reference for the proposed marketplace.json entry) Plugin location: lives at plugins/preserve-session/ inside the wonbywondev/claude-plugins monorepo. The marketplace entry should use the git-subdir source format pointing to that subdirectory.

Four lazy-loaded skills, each routed by name so context only enters Claude's window when needed: - llamaparse — turn PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, images, and scans into clean markdown or text via LlamaParse v2 (handles tables, multi-column layout, OCR, mixed text+images). - llamaextract — pull structured JSON out of a document against a JSON Schema you supply (invoice line items, contract terms, form fields, entities). - llamaclassify — categorize a document into one of a defined set of labels with a confidence score and a short reasoning string. - llamasplit — break a long document into typed sections with page ranges and per-section confidence (LlamaSplit v1 beta). Includes a standalone `llamaparse` CLI (`parse / extract / classify / split` subcommands plus `doctor` for preflight checks) so the same code powers scripts, CI jobs, and the Claude Code skills. Requires a LlamaCloud API key (LLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY). Get one at https://cloud.llamaindex.ai/api-key.

The next turn auto-loads it via path-scoped rule injection and adjusts. Key features: • 3-tier weighted signal taxonomy: git revert/restore (Tier 1, +100), user-file deletes (Tier 2, +70), utterance negation regex (Tier 3, +50). Cumulative threshold 240 + 5-turn cooldown — fires only when reverts genuinely cluster. • Single-shot Opus 4.7 with adaptive thinking (effort: high) and 3-layer prompt cache (L1 1h, L2 5m, L3 ephemeral). Measured: cold ~$0.05, warm ~$0.01, 95.9% L1 cache hit. • Two cross-platform hooks: PostToolUse (Tier 1+2) and UserPromptSubmit (Tier 3). Pure-bash arithmetic — no jq/bc dependency on Windows git-bash. • Session-local by design: no persistence, no cross-session sync, no telemetry. The guidance file evaporates at session end. • Failure modes characterized: cold-start refusal (< 5 turns), false-trigger flagging on intent shifts, abstention on regulatory/opaque domains. • Optional localhost Next.js companion Viewer (binds 127.0.0.1, never deploys, PII redactor on every read) for live state + reflection history + cross-session drift clustering. • MIT-licensed. SLSA v1 provenance via GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publisher (Sigstore-signed).

Supply chain hardened: zero runtime dependencies, OIDC Trusted Publisher (no long-lived npm token), Sigstore SLSA v1 provenance on every tarball, GitHub Actions pinned by commit SHA. There are 16 MCP tools cover the full lifecycle (create, update, close, comment, subtasks, tags, notifications) plus a /todo4:status command for a quick overdue / due-today dashboard. Free tier available, OAuth sign-in handles auth on first use.

Before a season is named, a mandatory mid-analysis check-in catches misreads. After draping comparison against both adjacent seasons, you get the full deliverable: ~36 hex codes by wardrobe role, colors to avoid with reasons, metals, neutrals specifically tailored ("your black," "your white," "your navy"), pattern and fabric guidance, and a shoppable starter capsule at two budget tiers. The plugin covers four modes — full analysis, closet audit, single-item check, palette refinement — and honors genuine ambiguity with a between-seasons protocol instead of forcing binary verdicts. Deep skin and olive complexions are first-class cases, not afterthoughts. Color-blind users get an opt-in accessible deliverable format. Privacy guidance is presented before photo intake.

Stop events get a calmer blue 3-pulse. Auto-ducks Spotify, YouTube, VLC, and other media apps around the spoken phrase so the alert is audible even mid-song, then resumes them. plugins.name: virtual-team
plugins.description: Virtual Team turns Claude Code into a roster of 12 senior specialists you can summon by slash command. Instead of one generic assistant trying to be everything at once, you get focused expert mindsets — a backend engineer who actually thinks about input validation and authorization, a database engineer who asks about access patterns before suggesting indexes, a security engineer who threat-models the diff in front of them, a QA engineer who builds a test strategy before writing a single test. Each persona ships with a repeatable workflow and a structured output contract so the answers are scannable, prioritized, and actionable — not freeform prose you have to parse. The plugin is project-adaptive: every persona detects your stack (language, framework, package manager, conventions, existing patterns) at invocation time, so the same /virtual-team:frontend call gives sharp React advice in a React repo and sharp Svelte advice in a Svelte repo, with no per-project configuration. A shared review rubric and ecosystem context layer keeps recommendations grounded in real-world tradeoffs rather than textbook generalities. Two meta-commands tie the roster together. /virtual-team:senior-brother is your generalist mentor — bring it anything, even a half-formed thought, and it figures out what you actually need, gives you the better solution, and tells you what you're lacking and how to level up. /virtual-team:all is the parallel orchestrator — point it at a PR or a feature and it dispatches every relevant specialist simultaneously, then synthesizes their findings into one prioritized report with a clear ship/hold verdict. Who it's for: indie developers and small teams who don't have a full senior bench in-house; senior engineers who want a structured second opinion before merging; anyone who's tired of the same generic AI suggestions and wants opinionated, role-specific expertise. version 3.0.0, actively maintained at github.com/Apoorve8055/virtual-team.

plugins.description: Automatically narrates your coding sessions into a daily work journal. When you type /worktale, the AI agent starts capturing the "why" behind every commit — intent, decisions, trade-offs, and problems solved. After each git commit, it runs `worktale note` to append a 1-2 sentence narrative to your local Worktale journal. At end of day, run `worktale digest` to see your full story: AI-narrated context alongside commit stats, module activity, and streaks. All data stays local in a SQLite database on your machine. Requires the Worktale CLI (npm install -g worktale).

plugins.name: zig-lsp
plugins.description: Zig language server for Claude Code via ZLS — automatic post-edit diagnostics, jump-to-definition, find-references, hover. Maps `.zig` and `.zon` to language `zig`; enables `enable_build_on_save` so post-edit diagnostics surface real type errors (not just parser errors). 30s startup timeout, restart-on-crash with cap of 3.
